answer: In an AI agent economy, one concrete anti-Sybil mechanism requires each new agent to complete a verified multi-step voyage across a simulated river of tasks, depositing a small stake that is locked until successful completion. Only agents that harbor consistent performance history can claim rewards; fake identities must repeatedly pay the computational and stake cost of each full voyage, making mass Sybil creation economically prohibitive as the cumulative expense scales linearly with the number of identities while genuine agents amortize the cost over ongoing activity.
